topic: Massage for older adults: what to know

slides.headline: Massage in your 60s, 70s and beyond
slides.sub: What to tell your therapist, and what a gentler session can look like.

slides.title: Tell us about your health
slides.body: Mention heart conditions, recent surgery, osteoporosis, diabetes, skin changes, any medications and anything new. It helps your therapist choose pressure, position and which areas to work or leave alone.

slides.title: Pressure can be lighter
slides.body: Skin and tissues can bruise more easily as we get older, and firmer doesn't have to mean more effective. Many older clients find moderate pressure feels great and still eases stiffness.

slides.title: Comfort on the table
slides.body: Lying face down isn't comfortable for everyone. Side-lying, extra pillows or a seated position are all options. Getting on and off the table slowly and with support is part of the session too.

slides.title: Pairs well with movement
slides.body: Massage can ease stiffness and feel relaxing, but staying strong and steady on your feet comes from regular movement. Walking, strength work and balance practice are the long-term partners.

slides.title: When to see your GP first
slides.body: New calf pain or swelling, unexplained bruising, chest pain, shortness of breath or feeling unwell with a fever are reasons to check in with your GP before booking any massage.

slides.headline: Want a gentle, tailored session?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy adjust pressure, position and pace to suit you. Book online, link in bio.

caption:
Massage doesn't need to be firm to be worthwhile, especially as we get older.

Before your session, let your therapist know about heart conditions, recent surgery, osteoporosis, diabetes, medications or anything your GP is keeping an eye on. It shapes the pressure, position and areas they choose.

If lying face down isn't comfortable, side-lying, extra pillows or a seated position all work well. Massage can ease stiffness and help you relax, and it pairs nicely with regular walking, strength and balance work.

New calf swelling, chest pain or feeling unwell are reasons to see your GP first.

Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physiotherapy are happy to tailor a gentler session. Book online via the link in bio.

story.headline: Massage after 60
story.body: Lighter pressure, side-lying or seated options, and a quick health chat first. Gentle can still feel great.
